lesson_title: One Till Slip, One Oven, and the Whole National Accounts
hook_text: Your gogo's grant is in the WRONG pile — and spotting why unlocks the entire national accounts.
clip_script: Imagine every purchase made in South Africa in a whole year printing onto one endless till slip. The national accounts are nothing grander than that slip, sorted into piles. Pile one, towering over the rest: households. Airtime, taxi fare, a bag of oranges, a washing machine. That is C — roughly sixty cents of every rand. In hard times the washing machine gets postponed and the oranges do not, so appliance showrooms go quiet months before food shops do. Pile two: the state's ordinary shopping — the teacher's salary, the clinic's vaccines, the ambulance's diesel. That is G. Now the classic mistake. Your gogo's pension grant is NOT on the government pile. Government bought nothing when it paid her — it moved money to her. The moment she buys bread and tea, it lands on the household pile, counted once, exactly where it belongs. And pile three, the special one: a bakery's new industrial oven, the highway, the wind turbine, the macadamia orchard. Things still working in ten years. That pile is the only spending that makes next year's till slip longer.
visual_style: An endless till slip scrolling upward, purchases peeling off into three glowing piles; a grant note tugged out of the government pile by an invisible hand and dropped onto the household pile; the third pile sprouting a skyline.
pacing: Brisk sorting beat, a freeze-frame on the grant mistake, slow triumphant zoom on the third pile.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and run the chain from GNE to GDP to GNI both ways.
